}} {{horizontal TOC|nonum=yes|align=center}} ==Incumbents== *[[Monarch of the United Kingdom|Monarch]] – [[Elizabeth II]] *[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] – [[Boris Johnson]] ([[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]]) ==Events== ===January=== *2 January – [[COVID-19 in the UK]]: A record high daily positive test figure is reported at 57,725, as the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|new strain]] of the virus continues to spread.{{cite news |date=2 January 2021 |title=Hospitals across UK 'must prepare for Covid surge', senior doctor warns |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55514363 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210102211657/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-55514363 |archive-date=2 January 2021 |access-date=2 January 2021 |work=BBC News}} *4 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***In a televised address, [[Boris Johnson]] announces a new, third [[COVID-19 lockdown]] for England, with people ordered to stay at home, and all schools and colleges to switch to remote learning from 5 January. This is expected to last until at least mid-February.{{cite news |date=4 January 2021 |title=Covid: New lockdown for England amid 'hardest weeks' |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55538937 |access-date=4 January 2021}} ***A new record high daily positive test figure is reported at 58,784.{{cite news |date=4 January 2021 |title=COVID-19: UK records 58,784 new coronavirus cases – highest daily total since pandemic started |work=Sky News |url=https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-uk-records-58-784-new-coronavirus-cases-and-407-deaths-12179186 |access-date=5 January 2021}} ***The UK's [[AZD1222|second vaccine]] against COVID-19, developed by Oxford–[[AstraZeneca]], begins to be rolled out.{{cite news |date=4 January 2021 |title=Covid: Brian Pinker, 82, first to get Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55525542 |access-date=4 January 2021}}{{cite news |last=Weaver |first=Matthew |date=4 January 2021 |title=Oxford man, 82, first in world to get Oxford/AstraZeneca Covid vaccine |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2021/jan/04/brian-pinker-is-first-to-get-oxfordastrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine |access-date=4 January 2021}} ***Most of [[COVID-19 pandemic in England|England]]'s primary schools reopen after the Christmas break, amid concerns over whether pupils should be returning during the current level of COVID infections. Most schools close again the following day.{{cite news |last=Coughlan |first=Sean |date=4 January 2021 |title=Uncertainty as primary pupils return in England |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/education-55525681 |access-date=4 January 2021}} ***The [[Joint Biosecurity Centre]] recommends that the COVID-19 alert level is moved from 4 to 5, indicating a "material risk of healthcare services being overwhelmed".{{Cite news |date=4 January 2021 |title=UK Covid alert level at highest rating as NHS at risk of being 'overwhelmed' |work=ITV News |url=https://www.itv.com/news/2021-01-04/uk-covid-alert-level-raised-to-highest-rating-as-nhs-at-risk-of-being-overwhelmed |access-date=5 January 2021}} ***[[Nicola Sturgeon]] announces tougher restrictions for mainland [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland|Scotland]] to contain the new strain of the virus, implementing a [[stay-at-home order]] from midnight and delaying the return to school for pupils until February.{{cite news |date=4 January 2021 |title=Covid in Scotland: Scots ordered to stay at home in new lockdown |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-55531069 |access-date=4 January 2021}} **The extradition of [[WikiLeaks]] founder [[Julian Assange]] from the UK to the US is blocked by a court in [[London]], due to concerns over his mental health.{{cite news |date=4 January 2021 |title=Julian Assange: Wikileaks founder extradition to US blocked by UK judge |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55528241 |access-date=4 January 2021}} *5 January – COVID-19 in the UK: The number of new daily confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the UK surpasses 60,000 for the first time since the pandemic began, at 60,916.{{cite news |date=5 January 2021|title=UK records more than 60,000 new coronavirus cases| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55550906|work=BBC News|access-date=5 January 2021}} *6 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***[[Secretary of State for Education|Education Secretary]] [[Gavin Williamson]] announces that [[GCSE]] and [[A-Level]] exams in England this summer will be replaced by teacher assessments, telling MPs he would "trust in teachers rather than algorithms".{{cite news |last=Coughlan |first=Sean |date=6 January 2021 |title=Teachers' grades will replace exams in England |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/education-55561838 |access-date=6 January 2021}} ***Another record daily case figure is reported, with 62,322 new infections. The daily number of deaths from the virus exceeds 1,000 for the first time since [[2020 in the United Kingdom#April|April 2020]].{{cite news |date=6 January 2021|title=UK reports highest daily COVID-19 deaths since April| url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-britain-cases/uk-reports-62322-new-covid-19-cases-1041-deaths-idUKKBN29B24W| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108005252/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-britain-cases/uk-reports-62322-new-covid-19-cases-1041-deaths-idUKKBN29B24W| url-status=dead| archive-date=8 January 2021|work=Reuters|access-date=6 January 2021}} *7 January – [[COVID-19 in the UK]]: Two anti-inflammatory medications, [[tocilizumab]] and [[sarilumab]], are found to cut deaths by a quarter in patients who are sickest with COVID-19.{{cite news |date=7 January 2021|title=Two more life-saving Covid drugs discovered| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55574662|work=BBC News|access-date=7 January 2021}} *8 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***A third vaccine is approved for public use, made by US company [[Moderna]] and offering 94% protection from the virus.{{cite news |date=8 January 2021|title=Moderna becomes third Covid vaccine approved in the UK| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55586410|work=BBC News|access-date=8 January 2021}} ***A major incident is declared in [[COVID-19 pandemic in London|London]] by mayor [[Sadiq Khan]], stating that the spread of the virus is "out of control" in the capital.{{cite news |date=8 January 2021|title=Covid-19: 'Major incident' declared by London mayor Sadiq Khan| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-55588163|work=BBC News|access-date=8 January 2021}} ***The highest number of daily deaths since the pandemic began is recorded at 1,325. A new record high daily positive test figure is reported at 68,053.{{cite news |date=8 January 2021|title=Covid-19: UK sees highest daily toll of 1,325 deaths| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55594107|work=BBC News|access-date=8 January 2021}} *9 January – [[COVID-19 in the UK]]: [[Buckingham Palace]] say that [[Queen Elizabeth II|the Queen]] and [[Prince Philip]] have both received the first doses of their COVID-19 vaccinations at [[Windsor Castle]].{{cite news |date=9 January 2021|title=Covid-19: Queen and Prince Philip receive vaccinations| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55602007|work=BBC News|access-date=9 January 2021}} *10 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***Professor [[Peter Horby]], chair of the government's [[New and Emerging Respiratory Virus Threats Advisory Group]] says on ''[[The Andrew Marr Show]]'' "we are now in the eye of the storm" and "it was bad in [[2020 in the United Kingdom#March|March]], it's much worse now."{{cite news |date=10 January 2021|title=Covid-19: 'Eye of the storm' lockdown warning as cases rise| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55609968|work=BBC News|access-date=10 January 2021}} ***[[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|Health Secretary]] [[Matt Hancock]] tells the BBC that everybody in the top four most vulnerable groups will be offered a vaccine by 15 February, while every adult in the UK will be offered one by the autumn.{{cite news |date=10 January 2021|title='Every adult to be offered vaccine by autumn'| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/world-55605009|work=BBC News|access-date=10 January 2021}} *11 January – Khairi Saadallah is sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of three men and the attempted murder of three others during a [[2020 Reading stabbings|stabbing]] in [[Forbury Gardens]] in [[Reading, Berkshire|Reading]] in [[2020 in the United Kingdom#June|June 2020]].{{cite news |date=11 January 2021|title=Reading stabbings: Khairi Saadallah jailed for park murders| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-berkshire-55622476|work=BBC News|access-date=11 January 2021}} *13 January – COVID-19 in the UK: The highest daily death toll since the pandemic began is recorded, at 1,564.{{cite news |date=13 January 2021|title=Covid: UK reports record 1,564 daily deaths| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55653161|work=BBC News|access-date=13 January 2021}} *14 January – COVID-19 in the UK: The government bans travel from [[COVID-19 pandemic in South America|South America]] and [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal|Portugal]] over concerns of a new [[Brazilian variant]] of COVID-19.{{cite news |date=14 January 2021|title=Covid Brazilian variant sparks South America travel ban| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55666198|work=BBC News|access-date=14 January 2021}} *15 January – COVID-19 in the UK: Boris Johnson announces that the UK is to close all travel corridors from 18 January to "protect against the risk of as yet unidentified new strains" of COVID-19, forcing all passengers travelling to the UK to produce a negative test result.{{cite news |date=15 January 2021|title=Covid: UK to close all travel corridors from Monday| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55681861|work=BBC News|access-date=15 January 2021}} *18 January – COVID-19 in the UK: Figures compiled by [[Our World in Data]] (OWID) show that the seven-day average for this week in the UK is the highest death rate per million population from COVID-19 of any country in the world after an average of 935 daily deaths were recorded, the equivalent of more than 16 people in every million dying each day from the virus.{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/uk-covid-death-rate-coronavirus-b1788817.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118135316/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/uk-covid-death-rate-coronavirus-b1788817.html |archive-date=18 January 2021 |url-access=limited |url-status=live |title=UK now has highest Covid death rate in the world |last=Cuthbertson |first=Anthony |date=18 February 2021 |work=The Independent |access-date=11 February 2021}} *19 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***Based on testing for [[antibodies]] against [[SARS-CoV-2]], the [[Office for National Statistics]] (ONS) estimates that 1 in 10 people across the UK had the virus by [[2020 in the United Kingdom#December|December 2020]] – nearly double the [[2020 in the United Kingdom#November|November]] figure.{{cite news |date=19 January 2021|title=One in eight in England had Covid antibodies by December| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/uk-55715793|work=BBC News|access-date=19 January 2021}}{{cite news |date=19 January 2021|title=Coronavirus (COVID-19) Infection Survey: antibody data for the UK, January 2021 | url=https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/healthandsocialcare/conditionsanddiseases/articles/coronaviruscovid19infectionsinthecommunityinengland/antibodydatafortheukjanuary2021|work=ONS|access-date=19 January 2021}} ***The highest daily death toll since the pandemic began is recorded, at 1,610.{{cite news |date=19 January 2021|title=Covid: UK records new daily high of 1,610 deaths| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55722168|work=BBC News|access-date=19 January 2021}} ***A record daily high of 343,000 people are given a COVID-19 vaccination.{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2021/jan/20/record-34300-people-in-uk-receive-covid-vaccine-in-one-day |title=Record 343,000 people in UK receive Covid vaccine in one day |last1=Sabbagh |first1=Dan |last2=Stewart |first2=Heather |date=20 January 2021 |work=The Guardian |access-date=9 February 2021}}[[File:Royal Navy COVID vaccine administration.jpg|thumb|[[Royal Navy]] personnel administering COVID-19 vaccinations in [[Bristol]] during early 2021]] *20 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***The highest daily death toll since the pandemic began is recorded, at 1,820.{{cite news |date=20 January 2021|title=Covid: UK reports 1,820 deaths as Johnson warns tough weeks to come| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55738174|work=BBC News|access-date=20 January 2021}} ***A record daily high of 363,508 people are given a COVID-19 vaccination, bringing the total number of first doses so far to 4,973,248 and 464,036 second doses.{{cite news |url=https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-nearly-5-million-people-get-first-vaccine-dose-as-uk-records-another-1-290-deaths-12194383 |title=COVID-19 vaccine: Record daily number of jabs given, as new UK death figures revealed |date=21 January 2021 |work=Sky News |access-date=9 February 2021}} *21 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***[[Glastonbury Festival]] is cancelled for the second year running as a result of the pandemic.{{cite news |date=21 January 2021|title=Glastonbury 2021: Festival axed 'with great regret'| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-55746293|work=BBC News|access-date=22 January 2021}} ***[[Arlene Foster]] announces that the lockdown in [[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland|Northern Ireland]] will be extended to at least 5 March, adding that restrictions may have to remain in place until after the Easter holidays in April.{{cite news |date=21 January 2021|title=Covid-19: NI lockdown to be extended until 5 March| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-northern-ireland-55704312|work=BBC News|access-date=22 January 2021}} **[[Storm Christoph]]: Five "danger to life" flood warnings are put in place across [[North West England]] and [[Wales]] after hundreds of homes are evacuated overnight due to widespread flooding caused by heavy rain and snow.{{cite news |date=21 January 2021|title=UK weather – Storm Christoph: Five 'danger to life' weather warnings in place in North West and Wales| url=https://news.sky.com/story/storm-christoph-thousands-of-manchester-homes-being-evacuated-amid-danger-to-life-flood-warnings-12194140|work=Sky News|access-date=21 January 2021}} *22 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***The [[R number]] is reported to have fallen to between 0.8 and 1 for the first time since the beginning of December 2020.{{cite news |date=21 January 2021|title=Coronavirus: UK R number 'between 0.8 and 1'| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55768033|work=BBC News|access-date=21 January 2021}} ***The latest analysis of UK data suggests that the new viral strain may be up to 30% deadlier.{{cite news |date=22 January 2021|title=Coronavirus: UK variant 'may be more deadly'| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55768627|work=BBC News|access-date=23 January 2021}} **Four men are jailed for the manslaughter of 39 Vietnamese migrants after they were [[Essex lorry deaths|found dead in a lorry container]] in [[Essex]] in [[2019 in the United Kingdom#October|October 2019]].{{cite news |date=21 January 2021|title=Essex lorry deaths: Men jailed for killing 39 migrants in trailer | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-essex-55765213|work=BBC News|access-date=21 January 2021}} *25 January – Online retailer [[Boohoo.com|Boohoo]] acquires the [[Debenhams]] brand and website for £55m after the department store went into administration in April 2020, but it does not retain any of its stores, putting up to 12,000 jobs at risk.{{cite news |date=25 January 2021|title=Debenhams shops to close permanently after Boohoo deal| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-55793411|work=BBC News|access-date=25 January 2021}} *26 January – COVID-19 in the UK: Boris Johnson says he is "deeply sorry for every life that has been lost" as the number of deaths from COVID-19 in the UK exceeds 100,000.{{cite news |date=26 January 2021|title=Covid deaths: UK passes milestone of 100,000| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55814751|work=BBC News|access-date=26 January 2021}} *27 January **COVID-19 in the UK: ***[[Boris Johnson]] confirms that schools in England will not be able to reopen to all pupils after the February half-term as planned, but could do so from 8 March "at the earliest".{{cite news |date=27 January 2021|title=Covid: English schools could return 8 March 'at the earliest'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55828952|work=BBC News|access-date=28 January 2021}} He adds that he hopes a "gradual and phased" relaxation of COVID-19 restrictions can begin in early March.{{cite news |date=27 January 2021|title=Boris Johnson promises plan next month for 'phased' easing of lockdown |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-55823364|work=BBC News|access-date=28 January 2021}} ***[[Home Secretary]] [[Priti Patel]] announces that people travelling from "red list" countries considered to be COVID-19 hotspots will be required to quarantine in government hotels, while anyone wishing to travel abroad will need to prove that they are making an essential trip.{{cite news |date=27 January 2021|title=Covid: Would-be travellers must prove journey is essential – Patel |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55821702|work=BBC News|access-date=28 January 2021}} *28 January – COVID-19 in the UK: A third vaccine, [[NVX-CoV2373|Novavax]], which will be manufactured in [[Stockton-on-Tees]], is shown to be 89.3% effective against the virus in a two-dose regimen, following large-scale UK trials. 60 million doses are secured by the government.{{cite news |date=28 January 2021|title=Covid-19: Novavax vaccine shows 89% efficacy in UK trials |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55850352|work=BBC News|access-date=28 January 2021}} *29 January – COVID-19 in the UK: A fourth vaccine, [[Ad26.COV2.S]], is shown to be 66% effective against the virus in a one-dose regimen. With 30 million doses ordered, Matt Hancock tells reporters that it could "significantly bolster" the UK's vaccine programme if approved by the [[Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency]] (MHRA).{{cite news |date=30 January 2021|title=Covid vaccine: Single-dose Johnson & Johnson jab is 66% effective |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55857530|work=BBC News|access-date=31 January 2021}} *30 January – COVID-19 in the UK: A record daily high of 598,389 people are given a coronavirus vaccination, bringing the total so far to 8,977,329.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55881092 |title=Covid-19: Record day for UK vaccinations as total nears 9m |date=31 January 2021 |work=BBC News}} *31 January – [[Flu]] cases are reported to have fallen by more than 95%, reaching the lowest levels seen in 130 years, believed to be due to the COVID-19 lockdown and new health habits.{{cite news |url=https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-lockdowns-and-new-health-habits-help-number-of-flu-sufferers-fall-to-130-year-low-12204516 |title=COVID-19: Lockdowns and new health habits help number of flu sufferers fall to 130-year low |date=31 January 2021 |work=Sky News|access-date=1 February 2021}} ===February=== *1 February **[[COVID-19 in the UK]]: ***The government orders an extra 40 million doses of [[VLA2001]], a vaccine from French biotech company [[Valneva SE]], for availability later in the year and into 2022.{{cite news |date=1 February 2021 |title=Covid-19: UK orders extra 40m doses of Valneva vaccine |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55887264 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203130125/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55887264 |archive-date=3 February 2021 |access-date=1 February 2021 |work=BBC News}} ***Door-to-door testing is launched, in an attempt to contain the spread of a new [[501.V2 variant|South African variant]] of the virus (later known as the Beta variant), after cases are found in [[Hertfordshire]], [[Surrey]], [[Kent]], [[Walsall]], [[Sefton, Merseyside|Sefton]] and three [[London boroughs]].{{cite news |date=1 February 2021|title=South African variant of Covid found in eight areas of England |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/01/south-african-variant-of-covid-found-in-eight-areas-of-england|work=The Guardian|access-date=1 February 2021}}{{cite news |date=1 February 2021|title=SA variant: Urgent testing after community cases found |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55889391|work=BBC News|access-date=1 February 2021}} **Online retailer [[ASOS (retailer)|ASOS]] acquires the [[Topshop]], [[Topman]] and [[Miss Selfridge]] brands for £330m, but does not retain any of the brands' 70 stores, putting 2,500 jobs at risk.{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/feb/01/asos-buys-topshop-topman-miss-selfridge-arcadia |title=Asos buys Topshop and Miss Selfridge brands for £330m |last=Makortoff |first=Kalyeena |date=1 February 2021 |work=The Guardian |access-date=11 February 2021}} *2 February **COVID-19 in the UK: ***[[Public Health England]] (PHE) says that the [[UK variant]] of COVID-19 has mutated again and that they are investigating "worrying" new changes. Tests show cases of the new strain have a mutation called [[E484K]] that is present in the South African variant.{{cite news |date=2 February 2021|title=UK finds more coronavirus cases with 'concerning' mutations |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55900625|work=BBC News|access-date=2 February 2021}} ***A study by the [[University of Oxford]] suggests that a single dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine]] could lead to a "substantial" fall in the transmission of COVID-19, and protection is 76% effective during the three months after the first dose is given, rising to 82% after a second dose.{{cite news |date=2 February 2021|title=Oxford vaccine could substantially cut spread |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-55910964|work=BBC News|access-date=2 February 2021}} **[[Captain Sir Tom Moore]], who raised over £32m for [[NHS Charities Together]], dies at the age of 100 after contracting COVID-19.{{cite news |date=2 February 2021|title=Captain Sir Tom Moore dies in hospital with coronavirus |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-55881753|work=BBC News|access-date=2 February 2021}} *3 February – COVID-19 in the UK: The number of people receiving a vaccine dose in the UK exceeds 10 million.{{cite news |date=3 February 2021|title=10 million people vaccinated in the UK |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/uk-55916020|work=BBC News|access-date=3 February 2021}} *4 February – Three people are killed, including an alleged assailant in a road crash, after [[2021 Kilmarnock incidents|an attack]] at the [[University Hospital Crosshouse]] and a related stabbing nearby in [[Kilmarnock]], [[East Ayrshire]], [[Scotland]].{{cite news |date=5 February 2021|title=Three killed after attack at hospital in Kilmarnock |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/feb/05/kilmarnock-stabbing-hospital-locked-down-as-police-investigate-three-incidents|work=The Guardian|access-date=5 February 2021}} [[Police Scotland]] say the incidents are thought to be connected but not terror-related.{{cite news |date=5 February 2021|title=Kilmarnock attacks: Two women and a man die in linked incidents |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-55948245|work=BBC News|access-date=5 February 2021}} *5 February **COVID-19 in the UK: [[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|Health Secretary]] [[Matt Hancock]] confirms the government's "ambition" to offer all adults over the age of 50 a first COVID-19 vaccination by the end of May.{{cite news |date=5 February 2021|title=Covid: All over-50s in UK to be offered vaccine by May |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55953848|work=BBC News|access-date=7 February 2021}} **One man is killed and ten people are injured after five stabbing incidents take place in the space of two hours in the [[London Borough of Croydon]].{{cite news |date=6 February 2021|title=Croydon stabbings: One killed and 10 injured in spate of attacks |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-55959214|work=BBC News|access-date=7 February 2021}} [[Metropolitan Police]] describe the stabbings as "needless and abhorrent" and say extra police officers will be deployed across [[south London]].{{cite news |date=6 February 2021|title=Croydon stabbings: 'Abhorrent' night of violence leaves man dead |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-55966362|work=BBC News|access-date=7 February 2021}} *7 February **COVID-19 in the UK: ***A not yet peer-reviewed study by the University of Oxford suggests the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine offers minimal protection against mild disease from the South African variant of the virus but does protect against severe disease.{{cite news |date=7 February 2021|title=Covid: Oxford jab offers less S Africa variant protection |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55967767|work=BBC News|access-date=9 February 2021}} Oxford lead vaccine developer, Professor [[Sarah Gilbert]], says a modified version of the vaccine capable of tackling the South African variant should be ready by the autumn, and that "efforts are underway to develop a new generation of vaccines that will allow protection to be redirected to emerging variants as [[Booster dose|booster jabs]]".{{cite news |date=8 February 2021|title=AstraZeneca races to adapt Covid vaccine to variant as South Africa suspends rollout |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/08/astrazeneca-races-to-adapt-covid-vaccine-as-south-africa-halts-rollout.html|work=CNBC News|access-date=9 February 2021}} ***The
